findings.quote: Those are rich multiples for a utility — peers typically trade in the mid-teens on forward earnings
findings.issue: The grounding surface carries no peer multiples: the Facts multiples block is labelled "company column; peers pending a peer data source" and the built report's multiples note reads "Peer multiples pending a peer data source." No peer forward P/E appears anywhere in the Facts or Context. "peers typically trade in the mid-teens on forward earnings" is therefore an invented figure, and it carries the central valuation argument.
findings.fix: Delete the fabricated "mid-teens" peer figure. Anchor the premium claim to something on the surface instead — the consensus target, the wide Street range, or NEE's own forward multiples against its 8%+ growth guide — and drop the measure-by-measure peer framing.
findings.note: Re-verified. multiplesCommentary still reads "those are full multiples, but they are not demanding against management's 8%-to-9% adjusted-EPS growth guide" and anchors to NEE's own 17.5x EV/EBITDA, 5.8x sales, 19.8x NTM, 18.2x FY27E plus the $98.39 consensus, $100.50 median and $55-$114 range. Grep across the judgment and report confirms no "mid-teens" token; the sole "peer" hit is the multiples table's own note ("Peer multiples pending a peer data source"), not a fabricated figure.

findings.quote: but NextEra has historically earned the gap by growing earnings faster than any large peer
findings.issue: "growing earnings faster than any large peer" is a comparative claim of fact with no peer growth data on the surface. The same ungrounded comparative recurs as "sector-leading earnings growth" (analystCommentary), "the best growth engine in the utility sector" (thesis), "a longer and higher growth runway than most large utilities offer" (growth.points[0]), "the standout growth story in the utility sector" (finalRecommendation), and "sector-leading growth" (meta.subtitle).
findings.fix: Either ground the comparison in a captured figure or state the growth without the peer superlative; use NEE's own record and the 8%+ CAGR guide and drop "faster than any large peer," "sector-leading," "best," and "than most large utilities."
findings.note: Re-verified. Grep confirms "sector-leading," "faster than any," "best growth," "standout" and "than most large" are all still absent from the judgment and report.

findings.quote: The current ratio of 0.53 is likewise typical of a utility that finances long-lived assets with long-term debt rather than working capital.
findings.issue: 0.53 is the trailing/TTM current ratio, but it sat inside a paragraph framed on the FY25 close where the balance table shows a FY25 year-end current ratio of 0.60, so the reader met two current ratios on one page with no signal which is which.
findings.fix: Label the period: "The trailing current ratio of 0.53."
findings.note: Re-verified. balanceCommentary still reads "The trailing current ratio of 0.53 is likewise typical...", distinguishing it from the FY25 year-end 0.60 in the table.

findings.quote: with $95B of total debt and a growth plan that outspends operating cash flow, higher-for-longer rates raise financing costs and can compress a multiple that had priced in growth
findings.issue: The same argument — $95B of debt makes financing costs and the multiple sensitive to higher-for-longer rates — was fully re-argued in balanceCommentary, risks.idiosyncratic[2], risks.systemic and finalRecommendation.body[1], paraphrase repetition rather than each section reaching a distinct view.
findings.fix: Make the leverage/rate mechanism once in balanceCommentary and have the later sections point back in words with their own angle.
findings.note: Re-verified. The mechanism is still stated once in balanceCommentary ("This rate sensitivity is the thread that runs through the risk section below"); risks.idiosyncratic[2] points back without restating $95B; risks.systemic reframes rates as the sector-wide driver; finalRecommendation.body[1] refers to it in words ("the leverage keeps the equity sensitive to rates").

findings.quote: Consensus embeds the plan, modeling revenue growth to $31.1B in FY26E and $34.7B in FY27E — a steady climb the premium multiple already reflects.
findings.issue: Several figures were reintroduced with their numbers in a second argue-section rather than referred back in words: FY26E $31.1B / FY27E $34.7B in both incomeCommentary and growth.points[5]; FY25 dividends $4.7B at 3.05% in both cashflowCommentary and management.capitalAllocation; and FPL's $12-$13B capital plan in three places.
findings.fix: Keep the first numeric mention and convert the later ones to word pointers.
findings.note: Re-verified. growth.points[5] still reads "modeling a steady climb in revenue and EPS through FY27E" (no numbers); capitalAllocation still says "the rising payout noted above" (no $4.7B/3.05%); the $12-$13B capex figure appears once, in cashflowCommentary, with companyOverview and capitalAllocation pointing to it in words.

findings.quote: A premium regulated-and-renewables utility with sector-leading growth, a transformative Dominion merger pending, and data-center demand as a new tailwind
findings.issue: The subtitle was 153 of 160 characters, leaving no headroom for the next round to edit.
findings.fix: Trim to leave working room, which also resolves "sector-leading"/"transformative."
findings.note: Re-verified. Subtitle remains "A premium regulated-and-renewables utility with a pending Dominion merger and data-center demand as a new tailwind" — 114 of 160 characters, dropping both "sector-leading" and "transformative."

findings.quote: For an investor who wants utility stability with genuine growth, NextEra is the premier way to own it; the price asks that the growth, and the policy backdrop behind it, hold.
findings.issue: Unearned hype adjectives the numbers do not carry: "premier way to own it" (finalRecommendation) and "transformative Dominion merger" (meta.subtitle).
findings.fix: Replace with plainer language and use "a large"/"a scale-adding" Dominion merger rather than "transformative."
findings.note: Re-verified. finalRecommendation.body[1] still reads "NextEra is a leading way to own that combination"; grep confirms "premier" and "transformative" are both absent.

findings.quote: FPL's rate-base growth is now supercharged by data-center demand
findings.issue: "supercharged" is hype vocabulary the house style rules out ("No hype vocabulary ... let the numbers carry the weight"); it is the same register as the banned "skyrocket." The 21 GW of large-load interest already carries the point without the intensifier.
findings.fix: Use a plain verb — e.g. "FPL's rate-base growth now has a new driver in data-center demand" or "is accelerated by data-center demand" — and let the 21 GW figure do the work.
findings.note: Re-verified. analystCommentary still reads "FPL's rate-base growth now has a new driver in data-center demand (management cites roughly 21 GW of large-load interest)". Grep confirms no "supercharg" token remains.

findings.quote: the pending all-regulated combination with Dominion Energy would add scale
findings.issue: "all-regulated" is a characterization the surface does not carry — the pack describes Dominion's "local operating companies" and the state/federal regulators reviewing the merger, but never calls the combination all-regulated. It also sits oddly against the report's own framing, which stresses that NEER is the unregulated, merchant-exposed half of NEE (businessMoat.segments: "exposed to policy and merchant dynamics the regulated side is not"), so a combined entity described as "all-regulated" overstates.
findings.fix: Drop the unsupported qualifier — "the pending combination with Dominion Energy would add scale" — or ground it to what the surface says (adds regulated utility scale across four states).
findings.note: Re-verified. analystCommentary still reads "the pending combination with Dominion Energy would add scale and, management argues, support 9%-plus EPS growth through 2032". Grep confirms the "all-regulated" token is gone.

findings.quote: This is a BUY on a utility with a genuine growth story
findings.issue: The intensifier "genuine" recurs four times and reads as a verbal tic (rubric 9, "no tic repeated past the point of notice"): thesis.body ("a genuine growth engine inside a low-growth sector"), scenarioCommentary ("keep the bear case a genuine scenario"), finalRecommendation.body[0] ("a genuine growth story") and finalRecommendation.body[1] ("utility stability with genuine growth"). Three of the four attach "genuine" to the same growth claim, and body[0] and body[1] are adjacent sentences of the final recommendation, so the word draws attention to itself.
findings.fix: Keep one "genuine" — the thesis is its natural home — and vary or drop the rest: e.g. "a real growth story," "utility stability with durable growth," and "a credible scenario" for the bear case, so the qualifier does not repeat down the page.
findings.note: Still open. This round's edit was scoped to the F-11 bear-driver rewording and did not touch this; grep confirms "genuine" still appears 4 times, unchanged — thesis ("a genuine growth engine"), scenarioCommentary ("a genuine scenario"), finalRecommendation.body[0] ("a genuine growth story") and body[1] ("utility stability with genuine growth"). Minor per the brief; left open.

findings.quote: Earnings still grow, but slower, and the stock de-rates to its 52-week low.
findings.issue: The bear driver named the 52-week low as the de-rate floor, but that grounded figure did not match the scenario's impliedPrice. The 52-week low on the grounding surface is $69.37 (quote.week52Low; snapshot "52-Week Range: $69.37 – $98.75"), while scenarios[2].impliedPrice is 67 — about $2.37 below the low the driver cited.
findings.fix: Reconcile the driver with the number: rewrite the driver so it justifies a move below the low rather than citing the low as the floor.
findings.note: Verified fixed. scenarios[2].driver now reads 'the stock de-rates to a new low, below its 52-week trough' — no longer naming the $69.37 52-week low as the floor, consistent with impliedPrice 67 (67 < 69.37). bearDownside 16.4% clears the 15% rule the low itself (13.4%) does not. Fair value 110*0.30+98*0.45+67*0.25 = 93.85 ≈ $94, +17.1% (matches conviction 0.1711). Target $75-$108 brackets base $98. F-1–F-9 remain addressed; Minor F-10 untouched.
